experiments.study_type: Assessment of surgical grasping-force-induced tissue damage using robotic forceps
experiments.procedure_text: Fenestrated grasping forceps grasped lungs, esophagus, aorta, liver, spleen, intestines with forces of 1,2,3 N for 1,2,4 min; histological tissue damage assessed.
experiments.procedure_text_evidence: the fenestrated grasping forceps of the Saroa surgical system were used to grasp the lungs, esophagus, aorta, liver
experiments.animal_counts_evidence: six adult male beagle dogs weighing 8.06 to 9.08 kg
experiments.test_system_evidence: the fenestrated grasping forceps of the Saroa surgical system were used to grasp the lungs
experiments.application_evidence: Saroa is a pneumatically actuated robotic system developed by Riverfield Inc.

endpoints.label: Lung tissue damage (hemorrhage/congestion, RBC count, pleural elastic and collagen layer thickness)
endpoints.evidence: we measured the area of hemorrhage and/ or congestion, red blood cell (RBC) count, and thickness of the pleural elastic layers and collagen layers

endpoints.label: Liver and spleen tissue damage (hemorrhage/congestion, RBC count, degeneration)
endpoints.evidence: we measured the area of hemorrhage and/ or congestion, RBC count, and area of degeneration

endpoints.label: Gastrointestinal tract tissue damage (hemorrhage/congestion, RBC count, mucosal erosion)
endpoints.evidence: we measured the area of hemorrhage and/ or congestion, RBC count, and area of mucosal erosion

endpoints.label: Aortic tissue damage (RBC count, elastic layer thickness)
endpoints.evidence: we measured the RBC count and elastic layer thickness in the intima, media, and adventitia

substances.name: atropine sulfate
substances.evidence: intramuscular injection of 0.05 mg/kg atropine sulfate

exposure.conditions: grasp the lungs, esophagus, aorta, liver, spleen, small intestine, and large intestine

experiments.exposure_evidence: with forces of 1, 2, and 3 N for durations of 1, 2, and 4 min
experiments.regulatory_evidence: in compliance with the "Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals" published by the US National Institutes of Health
experiments.notes: Grasping forces are mechanical loads, not chemical administration; no route applicable to the test intervention. Anesthetic/euthanasia agents listed as 'other' role.
